title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Follow-up to the reliability incident observed during the POC load tests. Reviewed root cause (autoscaler/queueing + backend 502s), current mitigations (rate limiting, retry/backoff), and agreed next steps including targeted load tests, autoscaler tuning, and a patch to reduce KV cache thrashing.
next_steps: Redwood: run focused load test with 2x traffic and share results by 2026-05-12
Acme: provide sample traffic profile and peak traces by 2026-05-11
Schedule deep-dive with networking/SRE to check LB timeouts by 2026-05-14
SE to share recommended autoscaler config and retry/backoff settings by 2026-05-12
action_items: Daniel Park - run controlled load test (2x) on dedicated pool - due 2026-05-12
Maya Lopez - share peak trace logs and traffic profile - due 2026-05-11
Liam O'Connor - validate LB timeout and client-side retry knobs - due 2026-05-14
Sarah Kim - send pricing/next-phase proposal and security docs link - due 2026-05-10
transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync. we wanted to focus on the incident from last thursday that caused timeouts and a bunch of 5xxs, sounds good?
[00:22] Rajesh Patel: Yep, we got the alert chain, it was pretty noisy — our users saw errors. we want to know root cause and what to do before we move forward.
[00:45] Daniel Park: Quick recap from our side: during the spike the autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough, queueing increased, upstreams returned 502/503 intermittently. there were also KV-cache misses that amplified latency for long prompts.
[01:10] Maya Lopez: just to clarify, the 5xxs we saw were more 502 than 500, right? some of the errors mapped to our internal routing layer.
[01:28] Daniel Park: yeah most were gateway-type errors. also we saw client retries firing at the same time which caused the traffic to re-burst. retry storms.
[01:50] Liam O'Connor: our side observed connections hitting the LB timeout threshold around 30s then recycle. some of the logs show worker processes restarted under high mem pressure.
[02:12] Priya Nair: thanks liam. we do have a reliability playbook, link in chat, and a short checklist for rate-limit and retry policy changes — I can drop that after the call.
[02:30] Sarah Kim: action items later, but high level items: (1) increase autoscaler burst capacity and decrease scale-up cooldown, (2) tighten retry/backoff with jitter on client side, (3) patch the model runner to reduce KV cache thrash.
[03:05] Maya Lopez: for the KV cache, is that happening because of prompt variability? our prompts changed structure during the test.
[03:25] Daniel Park: yes, prefix variability caused cache misses and more compute per request. also quantization boundaries for some model variants contributed to latency spikes.
[03:50] Rajesh Patel: what about rate limits — we bumped limits during the POC to emulate prod traffic, could that be related?
[04:05] Daniel Park: raising limits increased concurrency which stressed the scheduler; combined with the slow scale-up it led to queue growth and eventually LB timeouts.
[04:30] Sarah Kim: quick interjection — competitors were mentioned in your notes, but our focus is operationally making the POC stable; benchmarking vs others comes later.
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: i'm worried about the client-side retries though, some of our clients will retry aggressively. can we suggest safe defaults?
[05:12] Daniel Park: recommended pattern: exponential backoff with base 200ms, cap at 5s, max 3 retries, and randomized jitter. also prefer idempotent retry only for inference requests that are safe to repeat — or use a request-id to dedupe.
[05:45] Maya Lopez: noted. we'll check our SDK.
[06:10] Sarah Kim: on the infra side we captured heap dumps and trace spans; Daniel can share a condensed incident log.
[06:25] Daniel Park: yes i uploaded a lightweight incident trace, link in chat — note some labels were garbled by the transcriber, e.g., KV cache was recorded as KV cash in the logs.
[06:48] Rajesh Patel: haha, classic. any quick wins to reduce risk immediately?
[07:02] Daniel Park: immediate mitigations: lower concurrency per worker, enable per-customer soft rate limits, and set a conservative retry policy. a medium-term fix is autoscaler tuning and a KV cache hotfix.
[07:35] Maya Lopez: will the hotfix require model restarting?
[07:45] Daniel Park: no full restarts; it's a change to cache keying and TTLs, rolling restart of runners per shard should be fine.
[08:05] Liam O'Connor: are there observed differences between hosted vs dedicated pool here?
[08:20] Daniel Park: in hosted we had more multi-tenant noise; in the dedicated pool we saw the same behaviour once concurrency was high because the scheduler has similar scale characteristics. Dedicated gives isolation but you still need right autoscaling settings.
[08:46] Sarah Kim: Maya, can you share your traffic profile? peak qps, typical sequence lengths, and how often you hit long prompts?
[09:05] Maya Lopez: yes we'll share a sample. our peaks were short bursts to simulate end-of-day processing, sequence distribution skewed to 800-1200 tokens for a subset.
[09:30] Rajesh Patel: we also noticed spikes aligned with batch jobs starting — need to surface that in the profile.
[09:50] Daniel Park: good we'll use that profile for the 2x load test.
[10:10] Priya Nair: about security/compliance questions from last week: Sarah, you promised the security doc link?
[10:22] Sarah Kim: yes, posted to chat: https://redwood.ai/security-poc-pack and the SOC2 summary is in the same doc. also will attach the audit log example.
[10:45] Sofia Chen: thanks, product wants to know if VPC/private deployment helps here or just dedicated pool?
[10:58] Daniel Park: VPC/private helps for data residency and extra network controls; it won't eliminate autoscaler/retry issues but it gives you more control over LB timeouts and network policies.
[11:20] Maya Lopez: timeline-wise, we're evaluating Dedicated for next quarter if reliability stabilizes.
[11:35] Sarah Kim: understood. next, walk through the incident timeline — Daniel?
[11:50] Daniel Park: incident start ~ 13:12 UTC, scale events lag of ~45s, queue depth peaked at 1200 requests in scheduler, upstream 502/503s started at 13:13 and continued in bursts until scale caught up. memory pressure on some runners led to process restarts at 13:17. overall incident ~6 minutes of elevated errors then degraded behaviour for ~20 minutes.
[12:25] Rajesh Patel: can you convert the queue numbers to approx latency impact?
[12:40] Daniel Park: queueing added 300-800ms on average but for long sequences latency shot up to 10s+ and many clients timed out at 30s.
[13:05] Liam O'Connor: and then retries caused a second wave because clients didn't backoff properly.
[13:20] Maya Lopez: is there a way to detect retry storms early?
[13:35] Daniel Park: yes, instrument error rates correlated with client IPs and request-ids; if you see same request-ids reappear it's a red flag. our console has per-route error-rate dashboards — we'll share a custom dashboard for you.
[14:00] Sarah Kim: priya, can you note we need that dashboard link in the follow up?
[14:10] Priya Nair: yep will include.
[14:22] Rajesh Patel: a question on rate limits: during the POC we set a soft limit of 150 qps, then we upped to 300 qps; what should be safe?
[14:42] Daniel Park: depends on model and sequence length; for your sequence distribution i'd recommend starting at 200 qps with concurrency caps at the SDK level and adjust after the 2x test.
[15:05] Maya Lopez: ok we'll implement the SDK caps.
[15:20] Sofia Chen: will this impact cost projections?
[15:30] Sarah Kim: possibly short-term but reducing error/retry cycles usually lowers overall unit cost; we'll share an updated cost estimate after tuning.
[15:50] Rajesh Patel: can we prioritize autoscaler cooldown changes? that's the main lever we want to try first.
[16:05] Daniel Park: yes recommended: decrease scale-up cooldown to 15s, allow 2x burst nodes immediately, and increase target CPU utilization threshold to avoid over-eviction during spikes. we'll propose exact settings after the load test.
[16:35] Priya Nair: Danielle — small note, some of your notes from the last transcript had mis-attributed speakers; we'll verify names in the recording.
[16:52] Daniel Park: thanks, it's common with these transcripts, sometimes Speaker 3 becomes Daniel even when it's Rajesh, etc.
[17:10] Maya Lopez: any concerns about changing retry limits breaking some of our client workflows?
[17:25] Daniel Park: that's why we recommend a staged rollout: update SDK defaults, run internal smoke tests, then enable for a subset of traffic. also use a header to opt-out if needed.
[17:50] Rajesh Patel: about monitoring, can we get an alert rule for queue depth > 500 with rising trend?
[18:10] Daniel Park: yes we can set a rule and hook to Slack/PagerDuty.
[18:35] Sarah Kim: let's capture concrete dates: Redwood runs 2x load test by Tue 2026-05-12, share results same day; Acme provides traces by Mon 2026-05-11; follow-up deep-dive with SRE week of 2026-05-14.
[19:05] Liam O'Connor: fine. small question: is the KV cache change backwards compatible?
[19:20] Daniel Park: yes fully backward compatible. it's mainly TTL tuning and key normalization.
[19:40] Maya Lopez: will there be any downtime for our POC?
[19:55] Daniel Park: no planned downtime; rolling restarts but low risk if done during off-peak windows.
[20:12] Sarah Kim: ok let's recap the owners. Daniel will run load test and propose autoscaler config; Maya and Rajesh share traces; Liam validate LB timeouts; Sarah will send pricing/security docs.
[20:40] Sofia Chen: do we have a target for stable POC to decide Dedicated?
[20:55] Sarah Kim: if the next two tests are stable and error rates under 0.1% at peak for three consecutive runs we can move to Dedicated evaluation.
[21:12] Rajesh Patel: sounds reasonable.
[21:30] Daniel Park: i'll attach the incident trace and the proposed autoscaler json to the follow-up. also the recommended retry/backoff snippet for your SDK.
[21:52] Maya Lopez: please include the dashboard link.
[22:05] Daniel Park: will do.
[22:20] Priya Nair: final note on procurement: budgeting looks ok, Sarah will share the phase-2 quote.
[22:35] Sarah Kim: thanks everyone. any final questions?
[22:45] Rajesh Patel: none from me. thanks for the quick turnaround.
[23:00] Sarah Kim: great — we'll send notes and action items. see you next week.
[52:00] (meeting end)
